happening.headline: It begins, quietly
happening.line: Hormones are rising and your period may be late.

learnMore.title: Eating for two? Not yet
learnMore.govt: You need no extra food yet. Focus on folic acid, green leaves and dal.
learnMore.private: You need no extra food yet. Focus on folic acid, green leaves and dal.

govt: Set a daily folic acid reminder
private: Set a daily folic acid reminder

happening.headline: Your body is making room
happening.line: Breasts may feel sore and heavy.

learnMore.title: Foods to be careful with
learnMore.govt: Skip raw papaya, unboiled milk, alcohol and tobacco. Keep tea or coffee to two cups a day.
learnMore.private: Skip raw papaya, unboiled milk, alcohol and tobacco. Keep tea or coffee to two cups a day.

govt: Ask Viva which foods are safe now
private: Ask Viva which foods are safe now

happening.headline: Nausea may arrive
happening.line: Nausea, food dislikes and a strong sense of smell are common.

learnMore.title: Easing nausea
learnMore.govt: Dry toast or khakhra before getting up, small meals often, ginger and nimbu pani.
learnMore.private: Dry toast or khakhra before getting up, small meals often, ginger and nimbu pani.

happening.headline: Tired is normal
happening.line: Your body is building a placenta and more blood, so tiredness can be deep.

learnMore.title: Questions for your first visit
learnMore.govt: Ask about your due date, which tests you need, your tablets and the danger signs.
learnMore.private: Ask about your due date, which tests you need, your tablets and the danger signs.

happening.headline: Inside, a lot is changing
happening.line: Your womb has grown to about the size of an orange.

learnMore.title: Your benefits
learnMore.govt: Register early to get JSY and PMMVY cash support. Your ASHA helps with the forms.
learnMore.private: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, most employers give 26 weeks of paid leave for your first two children.

govt: Set a reminder for your first ANC visit
private: Set a reminder for your first ANC visit

happening.headline: Hold on, it gets easier
happening.line: Nausea often peaks around now.

learnMore.title: When vomiting is too much
learnMore.govt: Cannot keep water down for a day, very little urine, or dizziness: go to hospital.
learnMore.private: Cannot keep water down for a day, very little urine, or dizziness: go to hospital.

govt: Ask Viva how much vomiting is too much
private: Ask Viva how much vomiting is too much

happening.headline: Your blood is increasing
happening.line: Your blood volume is rising, so you may see veins on your breasts and belly and feel warmer than others.

learnMore.title: Iron for two
learnMore.govt: Eat iron foods with lemon or amla. Keep tea away from meals.
learnMore.private: Eat iron foods with lemon or amla. Keep tea away from meals.

happening.headline: Steadier days ahead
happening.line: Your appetite may start to return.

learnMore.title: Tired is not lazy
learnMore.govt: Your body is building the placenta. A short rest in the day helps.
learnMore.private: Your body is building the placenta. A short rest in the day helps.

govt: Ask Viva what happens at your ANC visit
private: Ask Viva what the NT scan checks

happening.headline: End of the first trimester
happening.line: The risk of miscarriage drops a lot.

learnMore.title: Telling your family
learnMore.govt: Share when you are ready, and ask for one clear kind of help, like cooking twice a week.
learnMore.private: Share when you are ready, and ask for one clear kind of help, like cooking twice a week.

govt: Upload your scan or ANC report
private: Upload your scan or ANC report

happening.headline: Welcome to the second trimester
happening.line: Energy often returns.

learnMore.title: Moving safely
learnMore.govt: Walking, stretching and pregnancy yoga are safe for most women. Stop if you feel pain or dizzy.
learnMore.private: Walking, stretching and pregnancy yoga are safe for most women. Stop if you feel pain or dizzy.

happening.headline: Iron and calcium start now
happening.line: Your body now needs more iron and calcium for the baby's bones and your blood.

learnMore.title: Making tablets a habit
learnMore.govt: Take iron at night with water, not tea or milk. Take calcium at a different time.
learnMore.private: Take iron at night with water, not tea or milk. Take calcium at a different time.

happening.headline: Your heart is working harder
happening.line: Blood flow is up, so stuffy nose or bleeding gums are common.

learnMore.title: Healthy teeth
learnMore.govt: Bleeding gums are common now. Brush twice a day; dental check-ups are safe.
learnMore.private: Bleeding gums are common now. Brush twice a day; dental check-ups are safe.

govt: Take your MCP card and show your logs at the visit
private: Share your summary before your ANC 2 visit

happening.headline: Your bump becomes visible
happening.line: Your belly grows steadily.

learnMore.title: Sleeping well
learnMore.govt: Sleep on your side, left is best, with a pillow between your knees.
learnMore.private: Sleep on your side, left is best, with a pillow between your knees.

happening.headline: Making space for two
happening.line: Appetite grows.

learnMore.title: Your free tests
learnMore.govt: Hb, urine, sugar, HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and an ultrasound are free at your health centre and PMSMA.
learnMore.private: The anomaly scan between 18 and 22 weeks checks your baby's organs. Ask if anything is unclear.

govt: Set a reminder for your PMSMA ultrasound
private: Set a reminder for your anomaly scan

happening.headline: You may feel a flutter
happening.line: Some women feel first movements around now, like bubbles or flutters.

learnMore.title: What a flutter feels like
learnMore.govt: Like bubbles, a light tap or a fish turning. If this is not your first baby, you may feel it earlier.
learnMore.private: Like bubbles, a light tap or a fish turning. If this is not your first baby, you may feel it earlier.

govt: Ask Viva when you will feel the baby move
private: Ask Viva when you will feel the baby move

happening.headline: Skin and stretch
happening.line: Skin may itch or show stretch marks.

learnMore.title: Itching to watch
learnMore.govt: Severe itching on the palms and soles needs a blood test. Tell your doctor.
learnMore.private: Severe itching on the palms and soles needs a blood test. Tell your doctor.

happening.headline: Halfway there
happening.line: Your womb has reached your belly button.

learnMore.title: Halfway check-in
learnMore.govt: What has helped you so far, and what worries you? Tell Viva.
learnMore.private: What has helped you so far, and what worries you? Tell Viva.

happening.headline: Moving more
happening.line: Movements become clearer.

learnMore.title: Cash support
learnMore.govt: PMMVY gives cash in instalments for your first child, and for a second child if she is a girl. Ask your ASHA.
learnMore.private: Plan your maternity leave dates with your employer now.

happening.headline: Your shape is shifting
happening.line: Your centre of balance changes.

learnMore.title: Bring your partner in
learnMore.govt: Invite them to a visit and share this week's card with them.
learnMore.private: Invite them to a visit and share this week's card with them.

govt: Set a reminder for your sugar test
private: Set a reminder for your sugar test

happening.headline: Swelling may start
happening.line: Mild swelling of feet by evening is common.

learnMore.title: Swelling: normal or not
learnMore.govt: Swollen feet by evening are normal. Sudden swelling of the face or hands, with headache, is not.
learnMore.private: Swollen feet by evening are normal. Sudden swelling of the face or hands, with headache, is not.

govt: Ask Viva when swelling is serious
private: Ask Viva when swelling is serious

happening.headline: The sugar test
happening.line: Your body handles sugar differently in pregnancy.

learnMore.title: About pregnancy diabetes
learnMore.govt: It is common and often managed with food changes. It usually goes away after birth.
learnMore.private: It is common and often managed with food changes. It usually goes away after birth.

happening.headline: Rest is part of the work
happening.line: Heartburn, back pain and poor sleep may grow.

learnMore.title: Better sleep
learnMore.govt: Use pillows, eat dinner early and light, and take a short evening walk.
learnMore.private: Use pillows, eat dinner early and light, and take a short evening walk.

govt: Ask Viva for better sleep tips
private: Ask Viva for better sleep tips

happening.headline: Learning the baby's rhythm
happening.line: You may notice the baby has active and quiet times, often active when you lie down.
chips: Active times when you lie down

learnMore.title: Learn your baby's pattern
learnMore.govt: A change in your baby's usual pattern matters more than any number.
learnMore.private: A change in your baby's usual pattern matters more than any number.

happening.headline: Third trimester starts next week
happening.line: Breathlessness on stairs and frequent urination return as the womb grows.

learnMore.title: Your birth plan
learnMore.govt: Decide where you will go, who comes with you, transport, money and documents.
learnMore.private: Decide where you will go, who comes with you, transport, money and documents.

govt: Ask Viva what a birth plan includes
private: Ask Viva what a birth plan includes

happening.headline: Third trimester: count the kicks
happening.line: From now, notice the baby's movements every day.

learnMore.title: How to count kicks
learnMore.govt: Lie on your left side after a meal and count every kick, roll or flutter. Most babies reach 10 within 2 hours.
learnMore.private: Lie on your left side after a meal and count every kick, roll or flutter. Most babies reach 10 within 2 hours.

govt: Take your MCP card and show your logs at the visit
private: Share your summary before your ANC 3 visit

happening.headline: Your blood needs more iron
happening.line: Anaemia is common in late pregnancy.

learnMore.title: Signs of anaemia
learnMore.govt: Tiredness, breathlessness and pale nails. Ask for an Hb test.
learnMore.private: Tiredness, breathlessness and pale nails. Ask for an Hb test.

happening.headline: Preparing your body for feeding
happening.line: Breasts may leak a little yellow milk called colostrum.

learnMore.title: Getting ready to breastfeed
learnMore.govt: Colostrum is enough at first. Your baby needs no ghutti, honey or water.
learnMore.private: Colostrum is enough at first. Your baby needs no ghutti, honey or water.

govt: Ask Viva how to prepare to breastfeed
private: Book a lactation session before birth

happening.headline: Practice contractions
happening.line: You may feel your belly tighten for a minute and relax.

learnMore.title: Practice or real?
learnMore.govt: Practice tightenings are irregular and ease with rest. Labour gets regular and stronger.
learnMore.private: Practice tightenings are irregular and ease with rest. Labour gets regular and stronger.

govt: Ask Viva: practice tightening or labour?
private: Ask Viva: practice tightening or labour?

happening.headline: Getting ready together
happening.line: Heartburn and breathlessness peak as the womb presses up.

learnMore.title: Help after birth
learnMore.govt: Decide who cooks, who helps at night and who takes you for check-ups.
learnMore.private: Decide who cooks, who helps at night and who takes you for check-ups.

govt: Ask Viva what to pack for the hospital
private: Ask Viva what to pack for the hospital

happening.headline: Packing the bag
happening.line: Pelvic pressure grows and walking may feel heavier.

learnMore.title: Free delivery
learnMore.govt: Under JSSK, delivery, medicines, food and transport by 102 or 108 are free at government hospitals.
learnMore.private: Confirm your room, insurance or cashless approval, and who to call when labour starts.

govt: Upload your MCP card and reports
private: Upload your MCP card and reports

happening.headline: The final stretch
happening.line: You may feel clumsy and tired again.

learnMore.title: Signs of labour
learnMore.govt: Regular painful tightenings, water leaking, or a blood-stained show.
learnMore.private: Regular painful tightenings, water leaking, or a blood-stained show.

happening.headline: The baby is settling down
happening.line: The baby may drop lower into your pelvis, which eases breathing but adds pressure on the bladder.

learnMore.title: The first hour
learnMore.govt: Ask for skin to skin and a first feed within an hour, even after a caesarean.
learnMore.private: Ask for skin to skin and a first feed within an hour, even after a caesarean.

govt: Ask Viva if walking helps before delivery
private: Ask Viva if walking helps before delivery

happening.headline: Weekly checks begin
happening.line: Your body is getting ready for birth.

learnMore.title: Know the danger signs
learnMore.govt: Can you name three for yourself and three for your baby? Try it with Viva.
learnMore.private: Can you name three for yourself and three for your baby? Try it with Viva.

govt: Take your MCP card and show your logs at the visit
private: Share your summary at your ANC 4 visit

happening.headline: Early term
happening.line: From now, the baby is considered early term.

learnMore.title: A birth companion
learnMore.govt: Government hospitals allow a woman of your choice to stay with you in labour.
learnMore.private: Ask your hospital who can stay with you in labour.

govt: Ask Viva when to leave for hospital
private: Ask Viva when to leave for hospital

happening.headline: Waiting well
happening.line: Sleep may be hard.

learnMore.title: Staying calm
learnMore.govt: Slow breathing, a short walk or music you like can help.
learnMore.private: Slow breathing, a short walk or music you like can help.

happening.headline: Full term
happening.line: Your cervix is softening.

learnMore.title: Normal or caesarean
learnMore.govt: Both are birth. Recovery is different, and both need rest and support.
learnMore.private: Both are birth. Recovery is different, and both need rest and support.

govt: Ask Viva about normal and caesarean recovery
private: Ask Viva about normal and caesarean recovery

happening.headline: Your due date
happening.line: Only a few babies arrive on the exact due date.

learnMore.title: Past your due date
learnMore.govt: Most babies arrive by 42 weeks. Checks keep you and your baby safe.
learnMore.private: Most babies arrive by 42 weeks. Checks keep you and your baby safe.

govt: Ask Viva what happens past your due date
private: Ask Viva what happens past your due date

happening.headline: Past your due date
happening.line: Your doctor will check you and the baby more often now.

learnMore.title: About induction
learnMore.govt: Medicines can help labour start. Ask why, how, and what happens next.
learnMore.private: Medicines can help labour start. Ask why, how, and what happens next.

happening.headline: Labour has started
happening.line: Regular tightenings, water leaking or a show mean labour may have begun.

learnMore.title: What to carry
learnMore.govt: MCP card, reports, ID, clothes, pads and baby clothes. Call 102 or 108.
learnMore.private: Reports, ID, insurance papers, clothes, pads and baby clothes.

govt: Reminder: carry MCP card and reports
Call 102 or 108 when tightenings are regular
private: Reminder: carry MCP card and reports

happening.headline: The first hours
happening.line: Your baby goes skin to skin on your chest and breastfeeding starts within the first hour.
chips: Instant love, or numb and tired: both normal

learnMore.title: The golden hour
learnMore.govt: Skin to skin and the first feed in the first hour help your milk and your baby's warmth.
learnMore.private: Skin to skin and the first feed in the first hour help your milk and your baby's warmth.

govt: Reminder: first feed within an hour
Ask Viva about the first feed
private: Reminder: first feed within an hour
Ask Viva about the first feed

happening.headline: Going home
happening.line: You are going home with your baby. Viva and your health worker are a tap away.

learnMore.title: Before you leave
learnMore.govt: Ask for the birth certificate form and your JSY payment details.
learnMore.private: Collect your discharge summary, follow-up dates and the birth certificate form.

happening.headline: The first week: your body is healing
happening.line: Bleeding (lochia) is heavy and red at first.

learnMore.title: How bleeding should change
learnMore.govt: Red for a few days, then pink, brown and finally yellow-white over the weeks.
learnMore.private: Red for a few days, then pink, brown and finally yellow-white over the weeks.

govt: Wellness check-in: how is your first week going?
private: Wellness check-in: how is your first week going?

happening.headline: Milk is settling in
happening.line: Breasts may feel full and hard as milk comes in.

learnMore.title: A good latch
learnMore.govt: Baby's mouth wide open, chin touching the breast, more of the dark area below the lip.
learnMore.private: Baby's mouth wide open, chin touching the breast, more of the dark area below the lip.

govt: Ask your ASHA to check the latch at her visit
private: Book a lactation session if feeding hurts

happening.headline: Finding a rhythm
happening.line: Your energy is still low.

learnMore.title: How was your birth?
learnMore.govt: Feelings about your birth matter. You can talk them through with Viva or a counsellor.
learnMore.private: Feelings about your birth matter. You can talk them through with Viva or a counsellor.

govt: Ask Viva what to eat while breastfeeding
private: Ask Viva what to eat while breastfeeding

happening.headline: Your body, one month on
happening.line: Bleeding usually stops by four to six weeks.

learnMore.title: Stitches and bowels
learnMore.govt: Drink water, eat fibre and do not strain. Most stitches heal in two to three weeks.
learnMore.private: Drink water, eat fibre and do not strain. Most stitches heal in two to three weeks.

happening.headline: Looking ahead to six weeks
happening.line: You may feel more like yourself, or still very tired.

learnMore.title: When can I get pregnant again?
learnMore.govt: Before your period returns. Breastfeeding protects you only if feeding only breast milk, baby under 6 months and no period yet.
learnMore.private: Before your period returns. Breastfeeding protects you only if feeding only breast milk, baby under 6 months and no period yet.

govt: Ask Viva which contraception is safe while breastfeeding
private: Ask Viva which contraception is safe while breastfeeding

happening.headline: Six weeks: a check for both of you
happening.line: Your 6-week check looks at your BP, wound, bleeding, breasts, mood and contraception.

learnMore.title: Your family planning choices
learnMore.govt: PPIUCD, Antara injection, Chhaya pills and condoms are free at your health centre.
learnMore.private: Ask at your 6-week check about contraception, sex, exercise and how you are feeling.

govt: Take your MCP card and show your logs at the visit
private: Share your summary at your 6-week check

happening.headline: Smiles and sleepless nights
happening.line: Most women feel stronger by now, though sleep is still broken.

learnMore.title: Only breast milk to 6 months
learnMore.govt: No water, honey or ghutti, even in summer. Breast milk is enough.
learnMore.private: Going back to work? Start expressing 2 to 3 weeks before. Milk keeps 4 hours at room temperature, up to 4 days in a clean fridge.

govt: Ask Viva about storing breast milk
private: Ask Viva about storing breast milk

happening.headline: Getting your strength back
happening.line: Hair fall is common now and grows back within months.

learnMore.title: Pelvic floor and tummy
learnMore.govt: Leaking urine or a bulge down your tummy is common. Daily exercises help; tell your ASHA if not better.
learnMore.private: Leaking urine or a bulge down your tummy is common. Daily exercises help; ask for physiotherapy if not better.

govt: Read: only breast milk to 6 months (Library)
private: Read: going back to work while breastfeeding (Library)

happening.headline: Six months together
happening.line: Your milk is still the main food as solids begin.

learnMore.title: Periods and pregnancy
learnMore.govt: Your period may return. You can get pregnant before your first period.
learnMore.private: Your period may return. You can get pregnant before your first period.

govt: Ask Viva about first foods for your baby
private: Ask Viva about first foods for your baby

happening.headline: Thinking about spacing
happening.line: A gap of at least three years before the next pregnancy is healthiest.

learnMore.title: Spacing your next baby
learnMore.govt: Waiting at least two years before the next pregnancy is healthiest for you and your baby.
learnMore.private: Waiting at least two years before the next pregnancy is healthiest for you and your baby.

happening.headline: A year of you
happening.line: Plan a check for yourself: BP, Hb and sugar.

learnMore.title: A check for you
learnMore.govt: From age 30, free BP, sugar and cancer screening at your Ayushman Arogya Mandir.
learnMore.private: Check your BP, Hb and sugar, every year if you had high BP or sugar in pregnancy.

govt: Set a reminder for your own health check
private: Set a reminder for your own health check

happening.headline: Your health matters too
happening.line: Keep your own appointments, not just your baby's.

learnMore.title: Your body now
learnMore.govt: Your body did something huge. Be kind to it, and talk to Viva if it is getting you down.
learnMore.private: Your body did something huge. Be kind to it, and talk to Viva if it is getting you down.

govt: Tell your ASHA if something has been bothering you
private: Book an expert if something has been bothering you

happening.headline: Planning ahead
happening.line: If you want another baby, talk to your doctor first about timing and folic acid.

learnMore.title: Planning another baby?
learnMore.govt: Start folic acid three months before trying, and talk to your ASHA.
learnMore.private: Start folic acid three months before trying, and talk to your doctor.

govt: Ask Viva about planning another pregnancy
private: Ask Viva about planning another pregnancy

happening.headline: Your first 1,000 days, complete
happening.line: Your health and well-being are worth tracking for yourself now.

learnMore.title: What comes next
learnMore.govt: Track your periods and your health. VivaMama stays with you for the next stage.
learnMore.private: Track your periods and your health. VivaMama stays with you for the next stage.

govt: Set a reminder for your annual check
private: Set a reminder for your annual check

card3.private: Say hello. Some mothers start a small diary for their baby from today.

card3.govt: Play soft music while you rest.
